description:
Upload local coverage + current source and get back what's still
untested — the core self-correction loop for writing tests without
waiting on CI. Works for Python (pytest-cov) and TypeScript/JavaScript
(vitest + Istanbul).

``coverage_kind`` selects the dimension: ``"unit"`` (default) is the
test-suite coverage flow described here; ``"browser"`` records an
independent per-function *browser-session* dimension from a real browser
run — any coverage format (Istanbul for a frontend harvest, pytest-cov
for a coverage-instrumented backend serving the browser's requests), no
junit. A branch's browser coverage is the **union** of what each
producer last reached — its wrapped suite, and each recorded test's
latest replay — and this upload replaces only the contribution of the
producer it belongs to, per language (a TS-only browser upload never
zeroes the Python dimension, and vice versa). It surfaces as
``browser_state``
(``exercised``/``partial``/``unexercised``) + ``browser_line_coverage_pct``
on each function and as the ``unexercised_browser`` gap in
``check_done``, and never changes unit state.

Browser and manual uploads are also recorded in the branch's session
ledger, so the Tests page can say what produced them. Pass
``session_id`` if you opened one; otherwise this upload becomes its own
session, attributed to ``agent`` — you.

Run your tests with coverage locally first:
  - Python:  ``pytest --cov --cov-branch --cov-context=test`` then
    ``coverage json --show-contexts -o coverage.json`` (pytest-cov's
    own ``--cov-report=json`` drops the per-test contexts)
  - TS/JS:   ``vitest run --coverage --coverage.provider=istanbul
    --coverage.reporter=json`` → ``coverage/coverage-final.json``

Pass a ``files`` map of {source_path: contents} for the files under
test, plus **exactly one** of:
  - ``coverage_json`` — a single parsed report (pytest-cov or Istanbul).
  - ``coverage_reports`` — a list of parsed reports, merged with
    same-file-later-wins; use this to send both a pytest-cov and a
    vitest report in one upload for a mixed-language repo.

IMPORTANT: the keys of ``files`` must exactly match the file paths the
coverage report records (relative to the directory the tests ran from).
If they don't, nothing matches and ``functions_matched`` comes back 0.

Stored and returned paths are always repo-rooted. If your tests ran
from a subdirectory of the repo (a monorepo package), pass
``path_prefix`` — the repo-root-relative directory the tests ran from
(e.g. ``"backend"``; ``""`` if they ran at the repo root). Omit it and
the server resolves the prefix against the repo tree best-effort, else
stores paths as sent. All reports in one call share one root — split a
multi-root upload into one call per root.

``functions_matched`` and the untested/partial lists count whole
functions only; React sub-units matched by the same upload are reported
separately as ``units_matched``, so those numbers stay comparable
across uploads and against a repo's own sense of its size.

Uploads are merged per language, so a TS upload never wipes a branch's
Python coverage (``functions_preserved`` reports how many rows were
kept). Upserts a single local analysis per branch, kept separate from
any CI run. Returns the coverage summary plus the untested/partial
functions and failing tests so you can fix them directly; the function
``id``s work with ``get_function_detail`` and ``get_generated_prompt``.

``repository_id`` is the GitHub ``owner/repo`` (a repo UUID also
works) — the same reference every other tool here takes.
name: upload_local_coverage
